title: Burn-rate-driven progressive throttling and per-tenant escalation policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define a deterministic, burn-rate-driven policy that automatically applies progressive throttling to tenants when their SLO error budget is consumed, and specify per-tenant escalation paths (notification, quota reduction, support-runbook, and optional manual intervention). Scope includes: metric definitions, three-tier burn-rate bands with concrete actions, API behavior during throttling, rollout gating for the policy, and acceptance criteria for production rollout. Out of scope: pricing changes, billing adjustments, and tenant contract negotiations.
background: We currently rely on coarse, org-level circuit breakers for capacity problems and manual runbooks triggered by alerts. Recent incidents (Jan 2025 spike in chat workloads) highlighted two gaps: (1) tenants can exhaust their error budgets quickly without automated, proportional protection of the global runtime; (2) engineering response is reactive and inconsistent. A burn-rate driven approach integrates SLO consumption into automated mitigation, reducing blast radius while enabling predictable UX degradations.
acceptance_criteria: Define burn-rate metric based on rolling 1h and 24h error budget consumption and publish formula (number of missing successful requests weighted by traffic vs allowed budget)

Three bands established: Green (burn-rate < 1.0) - no action; Amber (1.0 <= burn-rate < 4.0) - advisory throttling (per-tenant token rate reduction + warning header); Red (burn-rate >= 4.0) - enforced throttling (hard quota reduction, 429 responses for excess, and escalation to support)
Per-tenant throttling must be configurable by tier (free/startup/enterprise) and support an escape hatch for enterprise accounts (manual override with audit log)
Automated notifications to tenant owners, internal SRE rotation, and an incident channel must be triggered at Amber and Red thresholds with distinct runbook links

Telemetry: dashboards show per-tenant burn-rate, throttle actions, and user-visible error rates; metric names and tags defined for ingestion into observability (e.g., metrics: tenant.slo.burn_rate_1h, tenant.throttle.action)
Rollout gating: feature is behind a runtime-flag and rolled out to 5 pilot tenants, then 20, then 100 with automated SLO/latency guardrails at each stage
No increase in global 99th latency beyond defined regression envelope during pilot (regression envelope defined in rollout playbook)
Runbook and customer communication templates published and reviewed by support/solutions engineering
End-to-end acceptance test that simulates tenant traffic pattern and verifies throttle thresholds, notification, and override behavior
decisions: Use a burn-rate formula that compares observed error budget burn to expected burn scaled by request volume; maintain both 1h and 24h windows for short and medium-term detection
Throttle implementation will be token-rate based at the API gateway level for immediate enforcement; runtime will apply KV-cache hints to preserve model-state where possible
Tiered configuration: default conservative settings for free tier, lenient for enterprise with manual override logged to audit
Expose throttle signals in response headers (X-Redwood-Throttle: none|advisory|enforced) and a tenant-scoped metric to track actions
Progressive rollout controlled by feature flag and an automated gate that checks global error budget and pilot tenants' local SLOs

acceptance_test_plan: Create a sandbox tenant and generate synthetic traffic that consumes error budget at controlled rates
Verify burn-rate metric calculation matches expected values for 5m, 1h, 24h windows
Trigger Amber band: confirm advisory header, no hard 429s, internal notification created
Trigger Red band: confirm enforced throttling (token rate drop), 429 responses for excess requests, escalation channel pinged, and enterprise override works with audit log
Run pilot with 5 real tenants for 48 hours and measure global 99th latency and SLO regressions; validate rollback if guardrails breach
